draft.title: Ethical dilemmas in texts
card: An ethical dilemma is a problem with no simple right answer. A character must choose between two goods or between two harms.
Whatever the character picks, something is lost. A choice between right and wrong is not a dilemma, because one side is clearly the better one.
Writers use dilemmas to show what a character values and to make readers think about their own beliefs.
A careful reader weighs both sides and the reasons for each before judging. Quick verdicts miss what the text is asking us to consider.
draft.remember: A dilemma has two hard choices and no easy answer, so weigh both sides before you judge.

a.q: Which situation in a story is an ethical dilemma?
opts: A nurse must keep a promise or save a child in danger
A boy must choose between honesty and stealing a bike
A girl must decide whether to wear a red or blue jacket
A thief must choose between being caught and escaping
a.why: The nurse must choose between two goods, keeping a promise and protecting a child, and either choice costs something. The boy's choice between honesty and stealing has one clearly better side, so it is not a dilemma.
a.clue: Look for a choice where both sides matter and something is lost either way.

b.q: In a novel, Tariq finds his brother hiding stolen medicine for their sick mother. He can report him and see him punished, or stay silent and let the theft go on. Why is this a dilemma rather than a simple wrong?
opts: Each choice causes harm and each has reasons behind it
Tariq clearly should report his brother straight away
The theft is excusable because the mother is sick
Tariq's feelings matter more than what he chooses
b.why: Both options carry a harm: punishing a brother, or allowing a theft. Neither is clearly the better one, so readers must weigh them. Saying Tariq should simply report him is the tempting quick verdict that a dilemma asks readers to avoid.
b.clue: Ask whether either choice is free of cost.

a.best: A nurse must keep a promise or save a child in danger

b.best: Each choice causes harm and each has reasons behind it
